findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 4
Raise: Security. Case: normal use - A Windows user copies the suggested command for a repository-controlled workflow name. The new branch retains the Windows fallback at `src/forge/repo.py:403`, which places the name inside double quotes. A value such as `nightly$(calc).yml` therefore executes the subexpression when pasted into PowerShell, rather than remaining a literal filename. `src/forge/fullrun.py:17` passes the configured name to this helper, and `docs/start.md:43` directs Windows users to PowerShell. The same helper also quotes worker notes and review reasons. The coordinator required names needing quotes to remain safe; [PowerShell evaluates expressions inside double-quoted strings](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/powershell/module/microsoft.powershell.core/about/about_quoting_rules?view=powershell-7).
(floor: Security)
Adds work: protect shell-sensitive Windows arguments; F 1 x H 3 = 3; 2 x C = 4.
findings.title: Protect quoted Windows arguments from PowerShell evaluation

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 1, Harm 1
Raise: Not done. Case: normal use - A client names its workflow `nightly+tests.yml`. This filename is safe as an unquoted argument, but the new character class excludes `+`, so Windows prints `"nightly+tests.yml"` while POSIX prints `nightly+tests.yml`. The named proof tests only `nightly.yml` as a plain filename and therefore passes with this mismatch. [CPython's POSIX quoting](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/3.11/Lib/shlex.py) leaves `+` unquoted.
findings.title: Not done: The printed nightly full-run command has no quotes around a plain file name, and it is the same on Windows as on other systems.

findings.body:
Gain 2, Work 2, Harm 1
Raise: Test. Case: normal use - A maintainer moves the unchanged quoting implementation into a helper and runs the pull request tests. The launcher rebuilds `repo.quote` with a substituted global `os`, so a delegated helper still sees the real host platform; the simulated Windows cases then fail on Linux despite unchanged command behavior. This test depends on Forge's internal function and its globals, contrary to the test audit's requirement that behavior-preserving refactors not break tests. Exercise platform selection at a stable boundary while checking the real command.
findings.title: Gate: tests/test_next_step_argument_quoting.py::test_1_nightly_next_command_quotes_only_when_needed

why: On Windows the printed next step puts double quotes around a plain file name, so the Windows platform run fails two nightly-setting tests and blocks the release.
